findings.claim: Yet Syal makes her sympathetic too: Ruth's performance is a desperate attempt to construct an identity...
findings.truth: The author of Never Let Me Go is Kazuo Ishiguro. "Syal" is Meera Syal, author of Anita and Me - a different set text. A student who names Syal as the writer loses AO1 and AO2 credit.

findings.claim: Miss Emily quoted as: "We didn't have the Gallery to look into your souls. We had the Gallery to see if you had souls at all." (also in flashcard 7)
findings.truth: Miss Emily's real line (ch. 22) is: "We took away your art because we thought it would reveal your souls. Or to put it more finely, we did it to prove you had souls at all." The lesson version is invented wording. This is a closed-text exam, so students memorise and reproduce it.
findings.evidence: https://www.goodreads.com/work/quotes/1499998-never-let-me-go - verbatim: "We took away your art because we thought it would reveal your souls. Or to put it more finely, we did it to prove you had souls at all."

findings.claim: Same invented Miss Emily quotation used as the unit's headline 'Key quotation', in the quotation bank, in the key-fact box, in knowledge check 5 and in flashcard 2 ('to see if you had souls at all').
findings.truth: The real wording is 'we did it to prove you had souls at all'. The lesson tells students to memorise a line that does not exist in the novel.

findings.claim: "Kathy narrates his death with characteristic restraint: 'He looked peaceful enough.'" (repeated in L4 flashcard 9, L6 content_html and L6 flashcard 11)
findings.truth: Kathy is not present at Tommy's completion. Tommy asks for a different carer before his fourth donation, and Kathy only learns of his death afterwards. She cannot describe how he looked, and the quoted line is not in the novel.
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/never-let-me-go/study-guide/summary - Kathy "voluntarily stops being Tommy's carer before his fourth donation" and "bids farewell to Tommy as he gets ready to make his fourth donation"; the quotation appears in no quotation collection consulted.

findings.claim: "Kathy describes this as 'told and not told'" and "This phrase, used by Kathy..." (also L2 flashcard 4, L2 glossary, L8 quotation bank '(Kathy)', L8 flashcard 8)
findings.truth: 'Told and not told' is Miss Lucy's phrase, from her speech in chapter 7: "The problem, as I see it, is that you've been told and not told." Attributing it to Kathy in an exam answer is a speaker error.

findings.claim: "Kathy stands alone in a Norfolk field, imagining that all the things she has lost... might wash up on the shore" and "The field is empty. The shore yields nothing." (also flashcard 12)
findings.truth: The final image is a ploughed field with a barbed-wire fence along it, and rubbish blown against the wire. Kathy imagines that everything she has lost has washed up in that rubbish, and that Tommy would appear across the field. There is no shore.
findings.evidence: https://www.goodreads.com/work/quotes/1499998-never-let-me-go - "I half closed my eyes and imagined this was the spot where everything I'd ever lost since my childhood had washed up"; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never_Let_Me_Go_(novel) - Kathy "stares at a remote fence where windswept litter has collected".

findings.claim: Ruth's "deathbed confession" (L5 content x3, L5 knowledge check 2, L5 flashcard 8, L5 practice 4; L4 content and flashcard 4; L3 content and practice 4)
findings.truth: Ruth apologises during the day trip to see the stranded boat, while she is recovering from her FIRST donation. She lives on for weeks, has a second donation, and completes after that. It is not a deathbed scene.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/never-let-me-go/chapter-19 - the apology "occurs before Ruth's second donation"; https://www.gradesaver.com/never-let-me-go/study-guide/summary

findings.claim: Madame's phrase quoted as "the old kind world" (L6 content, L7 content x2, L7 flashcard 7)
findings.truth: The novel reads "the old kind of world": "holding to her breast the old kind of world, one that she knew in her heart could not remain". The dropped 'of' changes the sense and breaks the quotation.

findings.claim: "Tommy later finds a cassette tape... in a Norfolk junk shop - the tape Kathy lost at Hailsham"; L7 says "Kathy finds her lost tape".
findings.truth: It is a second copy of the same Judy Bridgewater album, not the lost tape itself. Both lessons contradict their own flashcards, which correctly say 'a replacement copy'.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never_Let_Me_Go_(novel) - Tommy "tells Kathy he wants to look for a copy of her lost tape"; https://www.litcharts.com/lit/never-let-me-go/chapter-6 - the tape disappears and is later replaced.

findings.claim: Every one of the 48 practice questions in this unit carries the mark split "AO1 (up to 8) / AO2 (up to 8) / AO3 (up to 4)".
findings.truth: The spec publishes no marking grids and no per-question AO split. It gives only whole-component weightings (Component 01: AO1 20%, AO2 17.5%, AO3 10%, AO4 2.5% of the qualification), and it states that AO4 is assessed in Section B only. An 8/8/4 split is invented. Options: (a) delete the three AO lines from all 48 'marks' strings and keep the band ladder, which is correctly scaled to 20; (b) replace them with one line, 'AO1, AO2 and AO3 (context) are assessed on this question'. Recommend (b), applied by script across the unit, because students still need to know which objectives are in play. Not hand-edited here: 48 near-identical whole-string swaps. ORCHESTRATOR: applied (scripted swap of the invented split; "in this section").
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md lines 1706-1750 (forms of assessment) and 1833-1948 (AO weightings table, AO4 in Section B only). No marking grid in the spec.

findings.claim: "AO3 (context) is assessed throughout - so you must weave in Ishiguro's purpose, the ethics of cloning, and the boarding-school setting's significance."
findings.truth: Part (a) compares the printed extract with an UNSEEN modern extract, and the spec gives no AO map for it, so 'assessed throughout' cannot be supported from the spec. If AO3 is not credited on the comparison, the advice sends students to spend time on context that earns nothing there. Options: (a) reword to 'AO3 (context) is assessed in this section' - safe under the spec; (b) leave, if OCR's published mark scheme is checked and does credit AO3 on part (a). Recommend (a) plus a check of the current specimen mark scheme before the wider unit is re-stated. ORCHESTRATOR: applied (scripted swap of the invented split; "in this section").
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md lines 1741-1750, 1833-1883; the spec carries component-level AO weightings only.

findings.claim: Five quoted phrases could not be traced to the novel or to OCR: Madame "stiffened - making a real effort not to shrink back from us" (L2); Miss Emily "We did the best we could" (L5 flashcard 10); Ruth "I should have been better to you both" (L5); Kathy "actually, maybe I'm not remembering this correctly" (L6, and L6 flashcard 4); Tommy's animals as "strange creatures" (L7); band descriptor "perceptive understanding of context" (L1 exam tip).
findings.truth: None was found in any quotation collection consulted, and the chapter 3 Madame passage is summarised elsewhere as her freezing and dreading being touched. Not edited, because the brief only allows a quotation to be called wrong once the real wording is in hand - except the Ruth line, which is removed by the F7 edit. Worth a second pass against the printed novel.
findings.evidence: Searched https://www.litcharts.com/lit/never-let-me-go/quotes , /chapter-3 , /chapter-6 , /chapter-19 , /chapter-22 and https://www.goodreads.com/work/quotes/1499998-never-let-me-go (3 pages). SparkNotes, GradeSaver quotes and CliffsNotes returned 403.

findings.claim: "Dolly the sheep (1996) was the first cloned mammal"
findings.truth: Dolly was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell; mammals had already been cloned from embryonic cells. The AO3 point still stands and no examiner would penalise it, so an edit is not worth re-narrating the lesson for.
findings.evidence: General science record; the claim is not load-bearing for any exam answer.

summary: Eight lessons checked; the exam framing is sound (closed text, 20-mark two-part Section A, no SPaG, no Paper/Component mislabelling) but the quotation bank is not: Miss Emily's Gallery line and Kathy's line on Tommy's death are invented, 'told and not told' is given to Kathy instead of Miss Lucy, 'the old kind of world' is misquoted, and Meera Syal is named as the author in lesson 5. Ruth's confession is repeatedly called a deathbed scene and the closing image is moved from a rubbish-strewn fence to a shore.
